title: Officer recalls struggle; Victim told to 'drop the knife,' jury told
article: A police officer involved in the shooting death of Robert Scott Carpenter told a coroner's inquest Monday that he never saw a fellow officer plant evidence or wipe blood on a knife.
Const. Rory Bennett, the first of several officers expected to take the stand this week, testified he "heard a loud bang" when he arrived last Oct. 30 at Carpenter's McCurdy Drive home.
Bennett, Const. Viktor Burany and Const. Matthew Capel-Cure were initially dispatched to the wrong address after a 911 call was made by Carpenter's common-law wife Lisa Stewart.
Bennett testified he and Burany raced to Carpenter's house with sirens wailing soon after 7 a.m. when the error was realized. Capel- Cure left before them.
Bennett said he drew his firearm and followed Burany into the house to find Carpenter laying on the foyer floor with his hands underneath him.

He said he heard someone say "Drop the knife" and Burany jumped on Carpenter. Bennett said Carpenter asked about a search warrant and a "serious struggle" ensued as he and Burany attempted to seize Carpenter's arms.

Const. Shawn McCurdy and Sgt. Bart DiPasquale beat Burany and Bennett to the scene. McCurdy has claimed responsibility for the shooting and forensic evidence supports him. Stewart maintains the fatal bullet was fired by DiPasquale.

Stewart insists her husband never attacked police with a knife and has accused police of planting evidence. The allegations first surfaced in a Nov. 14 interview with a student working for Patrick Ducharme, a lawyer retained by Carpenter's family.
According to transcripts, Stewart maintains a broken mirror caused DiPasquale's injuries and that blood was wiped on the planted knife.
Under questioning by Joanne Mulcahy, lawyer for the police service board, Stewart admitted she never saw the events occur but assumed they did.
Mulcahy asked Stewart how the jury could believe her ever- changing stories. Stewart retorted that the particulars hadn't changed.
Stewart, who referred to the shooting Monday as "murder," has maintained from the outset that officers punched and kicked Carpenter in the head after the shooting.
Bennett testified he saw Burany hit Carpenter in the head at least five times during the struggle in the foyer, but never saw anyone kick him.

Ducharme showed the jury a ring that Stewart testified Carpenter always wore and then played a video investigators made of the shooting scene. An object that may be a ring is visible on the floor a few feet away from a pool of Carpenter's blood, but the ring is on Carpenter's finger in hospital, according to autopsy photos.
